title: Joshua Link: $240M Cattle Ponzi — FBI Fugitive Now CONVICTED
summary:
Agridime cattle fraud: Joshua Link and Jason Link convicted in the $240 million cattle investment scheme — the Fort Worth cattle Ponzi case explained from the court record.
Joshua Link FBI fugitive, Jason Link, Agridime LLC Fort Worth: $2,000 a head, "guaranteed" 15-20% returns, 2,200+ victims.
Photo: FBI wanted poster (2026), U.S. government work, public domain.
On November 10, 2026, a federal jury in Fort Worth, Texas, convicted Agridime co-owner Joshua Link — a former FBI-wanted fugitive taken into custody at LAX in March 2026 — and his brother Jason Link. Prosecutors say Agridime collected over $240 million from more than 2,200 people who paid $2,000 a head for "guaranteed" 15-20% returns, and sold about 60,000 more head of cattle than it controlled. Sentencing is set for March 4, 2027; the brothers have not been sentenced.
docs_note: Documents shown are U.S. Department of Justice filings and press-release exhibits, an FBI wanted poster (FBI seal removed), and U.S. district court records in the SEC and CFTC civil cases (public domain). Indictment and SEC complaint statements are allegations unless the jury verdict or a guilty plea covers them. Photo of Joshua Link: FBI wanted poster (2026), U.S. government work. Victims are not named.
